turnDetection.mechanism: TRANSCRIPT/context classifier, not audio: livekit-plugins-turn-detector 1.8.3 -> base._EUORunnerBase.run() -> onnx/model_q8.onnx; returns eou_probability for the last token of the chat template. Framework rule (voice/audio_recognition.py:1603): end_of_turn_probability < unlikely_threshold => turn NOT finished. Sanctioned class EOUModelBase/MultilingualModel requires get_job_context().inference_executor (RuntimeError 'no job context found' offline), so the runner _EUORunnerMultilingual was driven directly and no room/JobContext/audio device/network was used. Context passed for the reported decisions: [assistant('明天上午有点小雨...记得带伞。'), user(fixture text)]; the no-context variant [user(fixture text)] was also measured (see NOTES.md).

interruption.mechanism: AgentSession/TurnHandlingOptions.interruption (livekit.agents.voice.turn.InterruptionOptions): enabled=True, mode='adaptive'|'vad', discard_audio_if_uninterruptible=True, min_duration=0.5s, min_words=0, resume_false_interruption=True, false_interruption_timeout=2.0s, backchannel_boundary=(1.0,1.0); endpointing via TurnHandlingOptions.endpointing (fixed: min_delay=0.3s,max_delay=2.5s,alpha=0.9). mode='vad' is local silero-VAD barge-in plus min_duration. mode='adaptive' uses livekit.agents.inference.AdaptiveInterruptionDetector: 25ms frames at 16kHz over a WebSocket to the LiveKit Cloud inference gateway (get_default_inference_url), threshold / min_interruption_duration=0.05s / max_audio_duration=3s / audio_prefix_duration=1.0s / detection_interval=0.1s / inference_timeout=0.7s.
interruption.missing: AdaptiveInterruptionDetector.__init__ raises ValueError without LIVEKIT_INFERENCE_API_KEY + LIVEKIT_INFERENCE_API_SECRET, and its InterruptionWebSocketStream opens a WebSocket to the LiveKit Cloud inference gateway (get_default_inference_url) to score overlapping speech. There is no local/ONNX interruption model in livekit-agents 1.8.3 (livekit.local_inference only exports EOT and VAD). The non-adaptive path (interruption.mode='vad') is pure local VAD, but it lives inside AgentActivity, which only runs once AgentSession.start(room=...) has joined a room, so it cannot be exercised offline either. A synthetic-audio interruption demo therefore needs either (a) LiveKit Cloud credentials + network, or (b) a real/loopback room plus the AudioOutput path. Missing: credentials, gateway network access, and a room.

blockers: Adaptive interruption (mode='adaptive') could not be demonstrated offline: AdaptiveInterruptionDetector() raises ValueError('api_key is required ... LIVEKIT_API_KEY') and its stream opens a WebSocket to the LiveKit Cloud inference gateway. livekit-agents 1.8.3 ships no local/ONNX interruption model (livekit.local_inference exports only EOT and VAD), and we are not allowed to use API keys, so this measurement is blocked, not worked around. The non-adaptive barge-in path (mode='vad') is local but only runs inside AgentActivity after AgentSession.start(room=...) has joined a room, so it is blocked by the missing room.

The sanctioned turn-detector class cannot be constructed offline at all: MultilingualModel() raises RuntimeError('no job context found, are you running this code inside a job entrypoint?'). The reported numbers come from the underlying inference runner (_EUORunnerMultilingual.initialize()/run()), which is a private class - it is NOT the same object as the documented EOUModel API, and a later M1 implementation still needs the JobContext/inference-executor wiring (or the new livekit.agents.inference.TurnDetector) to use it in a real agent.

No ASR is installed in this venv, so the end-of-utterance plugin had to be fed the fixtures' known transcripts. Whether a real Chinese ASR would emit exactly those strings (punctuation, '嗯' vs '恩') is unmeasured, and the transcript is the only input this model sees.

True end of speech is a DSP estimate, not ground truth: no transcript-level alignment or hand-annotated boundary exists. Thresholds were varied 3 ways (4x/6x/10x noise floor) giving a +/-20-30 ms band on 4 fixtures, but tests/audio-fixtures/followup-turn.wav is truncated mid-speech (no trailing silence; last 5 ms RMS 236 vs noise floor 44), so its true end of speech is only known to +/-107 ms and its 718.62 ms endpoint delay carries that uncertainty.

The turn-detector verdict for the backchannel is context-sensitive and only 2 synthetic contexts were measured: '嗯。' scores 0.00878 >= threshold 0.0066 (finished=True, i.e. WRONG) with no preceding assistant turn, and 0.003671 < 0.0066 (finished=False, correct) after an assistant reply. The behaviour under a real multi-turn conversation, and the true false-positive rate in a TV-filled room, are unmeasured. The absolute margin is also tiny (0.0066 threshold), so this model's 'probability' must not be read as a calibrated probability.

Backchannel suppression and false-interruption recovery (backchannel_boundary, false_interruption_timeout) could not be exercised: they live in AgentActivity, which requires a started AgentSession with a room.
